text: This course doesn't start from zero. If you've worked through Data Governance Foundations and Data Quality Management elsewhere in this catalog, you already have the base everything here builds on. Neither of those gets thrown out, both get extended.

Three things carry forward unchanged. Roles, data owners and stewards still own the datasets that feed a model, AI governance adds model owners and validators on top, it doesn't replace them. Policies and standards, existing classification and handling rules still apply whether a dataset ends up in a dashboard or a training set. Quality dimensions, the same six measures, accuracy, completeness, consistency, validity, uniqueness, timeliness, still define good data.

Three things don't have a direct equivalent in plain data governance. The model as a new kind of asset, a dataset sits still until queried, a model acts continuously once deployed. Training-specific data concerns, provenance, consent, and labeling matter more intensely because the data gets baked into the model's permanent behavior, not just read. Production behavior monitoring, a bad report gets corrected when someone notices, a model's behavior has to be actively watched for drift and misuse.

An organization that tries to do AI governance without working data governance first ends up approving a model's fairness testing while nobody can say where its training data actually came from. The foundation has to hold before the layer on top of it means anything.
That closes Chapter One. Next up: Chapter Two, training data governance, where the data-for-AI chapters begin.
